How much is a fishing trip on Koh Samui? | A shared day on a Thai fishing boat costs about 1,500–1,800 THB per adult in 2026; ours is 1,800 THB (child 1,300) with transfer, lunch and gear. Private fishing boats start at 10,500 THB for up to 3 guests, and a sport-fishing speedboat costs 32,400 THB for up to 10.
Do I need my own rod for fishing on Samui? | No. Rods, bait and lures are included on the shared day trip, and private boats include rods, reels, tackle and bait. Bring your favourite lures or reel if you like.
Can we cook what we catch on a Samui fishing trip? | Yes. On the shared day trip the crew cook fish from the morning's catch for lunch on board, and night squid trips grill or stir-fry the squid you catch.
Is night squid fishing good for kids? | Yes, it is the easiest fishing for children because squid bite readily on light hand lines under the lamps. Choose a trip that finishes by about 23:00, bring a jumper and keep life jackets on.
Can we fish in Ang Thong Marine Park? | No. Ang Thong is a national marine park and fishing inside it is prohibited, so boats fish outside the park boundary. The park is also closed to visitors from 1 November to 15 December.
What is the best season for fishing on Koh Samui? | February to September, with the calmest seas from February to April. From October to December north-coast trips are often cancelled, while private boats from the sheltered south coast keep fishing on most days.
What fish can you catch around Koh Samui? | Mostly snapper, grouper and small reef fish on bottom lines, with Spanish mackerel, trevally, queenfish and barracuda on trolling trips and squid at night. Bigger fish such as cobia and sailfish are occasional.
Is the catch guaranteed on a fishing trip from Samui? | No. Skippers choose spots by season and weather, but the Gulf of Thailand is heavily fished. Expect a fun day with small and medium fish rather than trophies.
